sources: https://reserveohio.com/OhioCampWeb/#!park/353 (ReserveOhio API ohiordr.usedirect.com: search/place PlaceId 353, search/grid facility 447 'Great Seal Campground' for 2027-06-15, 2026-11-17, 2027-01-12 and 2027-03-16, search/details for every unit on 2027-06-15, plus sites 001 and 011 on 2027-06-19, 2026-11-17 and 2027-01-12, read 2026-10-30)

values.note: Every site is non-electric: $23 a night, the same on a Saturday (June 2027); $19 off-peak (November 2026, January 2027). Plus tax and a $6.50 reservation fee per reservation. ReserveOhio's prices read 2026-10-30.

fees.source: ReserveOhio search/details for all 15 Great Seal campsites, 2027-06-15 (Campsite Equestrian Non-Electric and Campsite Non-Electric 23.00, Fee 6.50); sites 001 and 011 on Sat 2027-06-19 (23.00), 2026-11-17 and 2027-01-12 (19.00), read 2026-10-30

hookups.source: https://ohiodnr.gov/go-and-do/plan-a-visit/find-a-property/great-seal-state-park-campground ('The park offers a primitive camping area'; '15 non-electric sites'; 'Drinking water' listed as a campground facility) + ReserveOhio search/details (all 15 sites typed Non-Electric, no water or sewer hookup listed), read 2026-10-30

values.note: 15 primitive sites. Sites 1-10 are equestrian sites with horse picket lines behind them and gravel pads 48-58 ft long, back-in; sites 11-15 have no picket lines and no stated pad (site areas about 66-74 by 38-46 ft). Pets permitted on all sites.

sites.source: https://ohiodnr.gov/go-and-do/plan-a-visit/find-a-property/great-seal-state-park-campground ('15 non-electric sites'; 'Horse picket lines (tie lines) are located behind sites 1-10'; 'Sites 11-15 do not have horse picket lines'; 'Pets are permitted on all sites.') + ReserveOhio search/details (sites 001-010 'Campsite Equestrian Non-Electric', PullInTypeName 'Back In', Pad Length / Maximum Camping Unit Length 48-58, Pad Surface Gravel; 011-015 'Campsite Non-Electric', Campsite Size 66-74 x 38-46 ft), read 2026-10-30

values.note: Drinking water, playground; a shelterhouse in the campground is first come, first served when not reserved. No showers or dump station listed.

facilities.source: https://ohiodnr.gov/go-and-do/plan-a-visit/find-a-property/great-seal-state-park-campground ('Drinking water', 'Flush Restrooms', 'Playground', 'A shelterhouse, when not reserved, is available first come, first served.'), read 2026-10-30

values.note: ReserveOhio sells all 15 sites in November, January and March.

season.source: ReserveOhio search/grid facility 447 for 2026-11-17, 2027-01-12 and 2027-03-16 (all 15 units free), read 2026-10-30

values.note: 'Reservations are required and may be made online or by calling (866) 644-6727', up to six months in advance. All 15 sites are web-bookable with a 14-night maximum on ReserveOhio.

booking.source: https://ohiodnr.gov/go-and-do/plan-a-visit/find-a-property/great-seal-state-park ('Reservations are required and may be made online or by calling (866) 644-6727.') + https://ohiodnr.gov/go-and-do/plan-a-visit/find-a-property/great-seal-state-park-campground ('Reservations may be made up to six months in advance') + ReserveOhio search/details (AllowWebBooking true, MaxStay 14), read 2026-10-30

summary: Fees confirmed ($23 a night, all non-electric) and added $19 off-peak. Brief's question answered: non-electric, so hookups electric 0 / no water or sewer hookup. Added 15 sites (10 equestrian with 48-58 ft gravel pads, 5 without picket lines), flush toilets, year-round (all sites sold in winter), ReserveOhio deep link, reservations required, 6-month window, 14-night max. Pin fine (189 m from the centroid).
flags: Phone missing: the ODNR campground page lists (740) 887-4818, which the park page says is the Park Office 'Located at Tar Hollow State Park' - there is no separate campground number.

CRITERIA (light): 10 of the 15 sites are equestrian ('primitive camping area with features for equestrian campers'; picket lines behind sites 1-10). Neither ODNR nor ReserveOhio says the equestrian sites need a horse, and sites 11-15 are ordinary non-electric sites, so it reads as a primitive campground with horse sites rather than a horse camp. Facilities are thin (no showers, no dump).
